summary.intent: Work out what the team's USP is versus Lio and the other hackathon teams, set up Microsoft Teams alerts, evaluate the Monty/n8n automation ideas, and build an MVP of the Monty-based 'routines' feature for the ask-soony project.
summary.outcome: Defined the USP (anchored evidence, closed loop with real suppliers, phone/Teams reach, the specific Hwaseong find), gave Teams webhook setup steps, rejected n8n (license, story fit, time) and built the Monty routines MVP (routines.py, Routines.tsx panel) with dry-run, sandbox type-checking and tests; 173/173 tests pass and lint is clean.

repo: ask-soony config lives in ask-soony/.env (gitignored); the Teams integration reads ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK.
Backend is Python under src/ask_soony/, frontend is React/TypeScript under web/src/components/, with a backend lint step and a full test suite (173 tests).
Routines may only call a fixed set of building blocks: list open cards, read a card with evidence, carry out an option (same send path as Approve), notify, log.
Tests needed explicit inbox routing and an explicit 'free' flag so routines saw the right state; routine tests were debugged by inspecting what routines see.

code.finding: New module holding the Monty sandbox runner. Routines are agent-written Python limited to our own functions, with no internet or file access. Monty type-checks calls before execution, so a wrong call is rejected with a clean error, and dry-run mode sends nothing.
New Routines panel built on the Sheet component, with an on/off switch per routine and expandable code. It is mounted into the main UI.

workflow: n8n's Sustainable Use License limits use to internal business purposes, so it cannot be the base of a sold product; check licenses before adopting tools.
The Monty API (pydantic-monty 1.6) is large (worker pools, sessions), so reading the PyPI examples and probing signatures in the shell was faster than guessing.
Before wiring in agent-generated routines, test them on a state copy and in dry-run mode against the real inbox.
Piping output through tail can hide results, so re-run the command on its own when output is cut off.

friction: The procurementmag article blocked automated access, so the Lio comparison relied on the site, product page and YC page.
The Monty API surface was larger than expected and the attribute for captured output had to be discovered by probing.
Routine tests initially failed because of inbox routing and a missing free flag, which took several debug iterations.
A lint error on a long line needed a separate fix pass.
Output was truncated by tail during the first dry-run check.
open_items: Waiting for the user to paste the Teams webhook URL into ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK and say 'done' so the test Hwaseong card can be sent.
